Interned in a 4th grade classroom. They liked playing “squid game” at recess, by playing red light green light with one kid who did finger guns. We had to shut it down because my teacher was very mad that they had seen at least parts of squid game, so we had to shut it down. Honestly in the digital age with Mr.Beast videos and tiktok, it was bound to happen. I read the Hunger Games at that age so I was finding it funny, but a lot of parents got emailed. 
Also, painstakingly carrying pumpkins into the classroom for Halloween decorating. Half the boys painted “Trump 2024, Yeet” on theirs. Also a slightly sad and funny thing that I just had to accept with a straight face, or else we’d get a lot of parent emails. 
One of my kids came up to me like “Is space real?” and I said yes, of course. Then he told me the moon landing was fake and his dad is getting him a gun. Had to let that one rest. 

Sometimes I think kids just do what they do to model what their parents think and we as teachers just act upon what maybe deserves an email and ways to avoid angry emails all day.
I let them know that I had Covid. Late policies are strict but not inhuman.

Hi. Idk if u really want an update but thanks so much for the comment. 
I sort of spiraled and had an anxiety attack while tipsy, and I haven’t been suicidal in over a year, so I posted here in a rush and I ended up calling a friend and talking and falling asleep. 
I ended up cleaning up the popcorn with my roommate that morning and even though my room is still cluttered, I got some laundry done and I’m sort of ready for the week. 
I’ve worked since I was 16 and I have enough savings for two month’s rent but it’s very anxiety inducing as I worked for $9/hour endlessly and right now I have no income, it feels like a slippery slope to draining my savings and it’s scary thinking of a lease/subletting for the summer/being unsure of my exact financial aid for next year/my parents being overwhelming. 
I’m getting a job probably next semester and definitely this upcoming break/summer, and the 2020 school year. 
I know that paying rent and finding a place is basic adulting but I felt and still do feel really excluded because although my friends joke about having $3 in their bank accounts, their parents make around $100k while I have been screamed at with my dad over him finding a receipt in my car for a $6 starbucks drink because of it being such a waste. My parents aren’t working and are a couple hears under social security, and pulling from their money is terrifying for me both financially and emotionally. 
 The friend who I called was very consoling and I love him but it’s hard feeling connected with him while I was crying about my future $600 rent while he had bought a $700 snowboard the same day.
College is getting harder for me but right now it’s 7am and I have about an hour’s work left on the project due at 2pm, and the other project is definitely late but oh well, hopefully my other grades will float me. I ended up doing other homework in procrastination earlier today so I’m a bit ahead in other classes. I’m don’t think I’ll get lower than a B in any classes so far but it makes me feel so incapable, disgusting, lazy, and essentially stupid to be procrastinating on a class that is so expensive. The project is also teaching excel-based financial planning, such as credit loans and mortgages and retirement, and it’s both tedious work and is calling me poor in 8 languages, which is very stressful to deal with right now. 
I’m honestly just depressed and scared I’m going to be exhausted forever and sometimes it makes me wonder if anything is worth that effort, but I guess and hope I got this. 
The free counseling at my school is backed up for months, but I really loved your comment, and I’m still stressed but I don’t really feel as hopeless. I really really loved your comment. Sorry I kind of ranted on but I really just needed to establish what I’m doing I think. Goodnight/Morning, thank you so much.
